Shrub thicket types - Shrub thicket types are characteristic of localized mesic conditions in upland drainageways and along creek bottoms. The snowberry (Symphoricarpos occidentalis) type consists of dense essentially pure stands of snowberry up to about three feet in height. The boxelder (Acer negundo) - hawthorn (Crataegus succulenta) - chokecherry (Prunus virginiana) type is essentially a riparian community characteristic of permanent and intermittent drainageways.
Agricultural Types - Agricultural types consist of primarily of crop and hay fields with wheat, barley and alfalfa the dominant crop plants.

Disturbed Types - Disturbed types include abandoned crop fields (disturbed grassland), roadways, logged areas etc. where non-agricultural activities of man (other than grazing) have greatly altered plant community composition.
Wildlife
The Sarpy Creek area has been the site of a number of wildlife investigations since 1972. Detailed information is available in reports prepared by B.C. Research (1973), Ecological Consulting Service (1974, 1975), Westmoreland Resources (1975 o) Dames and Moore (1975), and the Montana Department of Fish and Game (1974).
Mammals - Fifty-four species of mammals that have been observed or may occur in the area of Tract II and Tract III are presented in Appendix F. Appendix F also lists some habitat and food requirements of these mammals.
